text: A bridge this long should snap. Here's why it doesn't.
A flat road this long, on its own, would sag and break.
So the road doesn't stand on legs. It hangs.
Rows of thin cables hold it up.
They hang from two huge main cables.
Steel cable is very strong when you pull it. That pull is tension.
The main cables run over two tall towers.
The towers get pressed straight down. That push is compression.
At each end, giant concrete anchors hold the cables back.
Each Golden Gate main cable is made of twenty-seven thousand, five hundred and seventy-two steel wires.
The road hangs, the cables pull, the towers push, the anchors hold them back. That's why it doesn't snap.
